metadata.explanation: Direct reduction of the trans-4-(Boc-amino)cyclohexanecarboxylic acid to the primary alcohol. The acid is a validated stock building block (InChIKey KXMRDHPZQHAXML-KYZUINATSA-N) and the cut matches a dataset record for this exact product; reported conditions for this acid are THF/MeOH-type, consistent with a borane or mixed-hydride reduction.
metadata.reaction_class: carboxylic acid reduction to primary alcohol

metadata.explanation: Boc protection of the trans-4-aminocyclohexanecarboxylate ester. Both precursors are validated stock items (Boc2O, InChIKey DYHSDKLCOJIUFX-UHFFFAOYSA-N; methyl trans-4-aminocyclohexanecarboxylate, InChIKey FFKGMXGWLOPOAO-LJGSYFOKSA-N) and the cut is dataset-supported (matched record with Et3N/MeOH-type base conditions).

Reduction of the methyl ester to the primary alcohol; the ester cut is a distinct first disconnection from route 1 and is dataset-supported for this exact target. The ester precursor is itself made in one further step from a validated stock amine.

metadata.explanation: Strecker-type disconnection of the quaternary aminonitrile: 1-benzylpiperidin-4-one condenses with aniline to the imine, then TMSCN adds cyanide to the imine giving the alpha-aminonitrile bearing the aryl-NH and C-CN at the former carbonyl carbon. Atom inventory conserved on validation; all three leaves are exact stock hits.

precursor_roles.O=C1CCN(Cc2ccccc2)CC1: ketone electrophile (former carbonyl carbon becomes quaternary C)

metadata.explanation: Amide C–N disconnection: acylate the pyrrolidine nitrogen of the secondary amine with a cyanoacetyl unit. Cyanoacetic acid is a cheap, in-stock acyl donor and standard peptide-type coupling conditions (EDC/HOBt or DCC, or via the acid chloride) deliver the cyanoacetamide without touching the tertiary N-aryl amine.

literature.note: PoC/Cl acylation of cyclic amines precedented, e.g. US05932595 Cbz-Cl + 4-hydroxypiperidine

literature.note: ClC(O)OR/acid + cyclic amine acylation precedented, e.g. US07741322B2

metadata.explanation: Aryl C–N (SNAr/Buchwald) disconnection: 4-chloro-7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine is a stock heteroaryl halide; displacement by the hindered secondary amine (N-methylation step) installs the N-Me adenine-type unit. Chloro-pyrimidine SNAr with amines on this scaffold is well precedented; the pre-formed amide side chain survives the coupling.

literature.note: amine + heteroaryl halide couplings precedented (e.g. US20120295874A1)

metadata.explanation: Direct reductive amination of the 1,4-dioxaspiro ketone installs the primary amine in a single step. Ketone O=C1CCC2(CC1)OCCO2 and ammonia are both confirmed exact stock hits; atom inventory for C8H15NO2 is conserved. Analogue conditions from the frozen set (amine/NH3 with reducing agent) support the transformation class, though no exact dataset reaction matched this specific cut, so confidence is moderate.
Condensation of the spirocyclohexanone with hydroxylamine gives the oxime. Both precursors (ketone and NH2OH) are confirmed exact stock hits; atom inventory is balanced for the intermediate oxime.

Oxime route: the spiro ketone is converted to the oxime (NH2OH, exact stock hit) then reduced to the primary amine in a second step. Two-step sequence targeting C8H15NO2. Oxime formation is a classic condensation; oxime-to-amine reduction is a standard transformation. No exact frozen dataset reaction matched either cut, so confidence is moderate; oxime intermediate is not a stock leaf and is expanded.

precursor_roles.ON=C1CCC2(CC1)OCCO2: oxime intermediate reduced to the primary amine
